articles.title: Rochdale businesses urged to back Denehurst House in £30-a-month veterans challenge
articles.excerpt: A Rochdale veterans support organisation is asking 100 local businesses to pledge £30 a month to help keep Denehurst House operational and support former service personnel in need.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale veterans support organisation has launched a drive to recruit 100 local businesses willing to pledge £30 a month towards keeping Denehurst House operational.

Get Together After Serving CIC, which is behind the campaign, says Denehurst House provides support for veterans including emergency housing, hot meals and mental health support. The organisation is promoting the appeal as the Rochdale 100 Businesses Challenge and is asking firms across the borough to make a regular monthly contribution.

If all 100 places are filled, the campaign would generate £3,000 each month in pledged support, equivalent to £36,000 over a full year if every business remained involved for 12 months. The appeal describes the contribution as a relatively small commitment for an individual business which, collectively, could make a significant difference to the service.

Campaign material highlights community spirit, warm meals and local businesses working together, with the message: 'Together, we keep Denehurst House operational.' It also says the project aims to provide a lifeline to veterans when they need it most.

The initiative is seeking support from companies of all sizes rather than relying on a handful of major donors. That model would spread the cost across the local business community while giving Denehurst House a more predictable stream of recurring income.

Local businesses interested in joining the challenge are being asked to contact Get Together After Serving CIC by emailing hello@gtascic.co.uk.

Rochdale Daily is publishing the appeal as today's front-page community story to help local firms understand what is being requested, how the funding model works and how they can take part.

articles.title: Search Underway for Missing 64-Year-Old Man Last Seen in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Greater Manchester Police are appealing for information regarding a missing man, James, who was last seen on Albert Royds Street in Rochdale on August 4.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

17:42, 14 August 2026

Greater Manchester Police are appealing for information regarding the whereabouts of James, a 64-year-old man who was last seen on Albert Royds Street in Rochdale on August 4.

16:35, 14 August 2026

Greater Manchester Police are appealing for information regarding James, a 64-year-old man who went missing after being last seen on Albert Royds Street in Rochdale on August 4.

14:25, 14 August 2026

Greater Manchester Police are appealing for information regarding a missing man, James, who was last seen on Albert Royds Street in Rochdale on August 4.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) have launched an appeal for information regarding a missing man from Rochdale. James, aged 64, was last seen on Albert Royds Street at around midday on Tuesday, August 4, 2026.

James is described as white, approximately 5 feet 6 inches tall, of slim build, and has dark hair. He is known to wear skinny jeans and occasionally a bobble hat. Officers have expressed increasing concern for his welfare and are eager to ensure he is safe and well.

The police are urging anyone who may have seen James or has information about his whereabouts to come forward. A spokesperson for GMP stated, "Can you help police find missing James?"

Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 0161 856 8643, quoting reference number MSP/06PP/0001307/26. The appeal was issued on August 14, 2026, as the search for James continues.

articles.title: Service Changes on Rochdale Line Due to Planned Works
articles.excerpt: Planned works on the Rochdale line will result in service changes this weekend, with further disruptions expected until 28 August. Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has announced that planned works will affect services on the Rochdale line this weekend, specifically on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August. These works are part of ongoing improvements in the city centre and along the Rochdale line, which will continue until Friday 28 August.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys in advance, as these changes may impact travel times and service availability. TfGM has not specified the exact nature of the service changes, but they are likely to affect both tram and train services along the line.

In addition to the Rochdale line works, there are also ongoing issues at several tram stops. The lifts at Failsworth and Etihad Campus tram stops are currently out of service, meaning there is no step-free access available. Passengers needing step-free access are advised to travel to Hollinwood or Velopark tram stops instead. For assistance, customers can contact the Metrolink customer service centre at 0161 244 1000.

Passengers are encouraged to check the TfGM travel alerts page for the latest updates and further information regarding the planned works and any other service disruptions. The contact centre is available from 7am to 8pm on weekdays and from 8am to 8pm on weekends and bank holidays.

articles.title: New Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig visits Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Newly elected Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig is visiting Rochdale today as she begins work across the city-region following her victory in last month's mayoral by-election.
articles.content_html:
Newly elected Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig is visiting Rochdale today, bringing the new city-region mayor to the borough during the opening days of her term.

Craig was elected at the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election on 30 July, succeeding Andy Burnham after his return to Westminster. She became the first woman to hold the Greater Manchester mayoralty.

The visit puts Rochdale among the places receiving early attention from the new mayor as she begins the job of representing all ten Greater Manchester boroughs.

At the time of publication, no detailed public itinerary or standalone press release about today's Rochdale visit had been published on the Greater Manchester Combined Authority news pages. Rochdale Daily has checked publicly available material from the mayoral and GMCA press operation and will update this article if further details, photographs or statements are released.

Craig arrives in Rochdale having campaigned on a platform that included expanding the Bee Network, freezing bus fares and extending free bus travel to young people aged 11 to 18. She has also placed housing, economic growth and reducing inequalities among the central issues facing Greater Manchester.

Those priorities are particularly relevant to Rochdale, where transport connectivity, town-centre investment, housing and access to opportunity remain major local issues.

Before becoming mayor, Craig led Manchester City Council from December 2021 and held Greater Manchester responsibilities for economy, business and inclusive growth. She was awarded an OBE in March 2026 for services to local government.

Her election followed the departure of Andy Burnham from the mayoralty. Craig won the contest after the count proceeded to a second round, defeating Reform UK's Sian Astley.

Today's Rochdale visit will therefore be watched for signs of how the new mayor intends to translate her city-region promises into action for individual boroughs outside Manchester city centre.

Rochdale Daily will add any confirmed detail released by the mayor's press team about the purpose of the visit, people she met or commitments made while in the borough.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Netball launched as Rochdale Netball Club joins Dale family
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Netball Club is becoming Rochdale AFC Netball in a new partnership with Rochdale AFC and its Community Trust, bringing nearly 200 weekly players into the club's wider sporting family.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Netball Club is joining the Rochdale AFC family under a new identity as Rochdale AFC Netball, in a partnership designed to grow the sport and create more opportunities for women, girls and the wider community across the borough.

The agreement brings together Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and one of the borough's established community sports clubs under the wider 'Our Teams' banner.

Rochdale Netball Club currently runs teams from under-six level through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court each week. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the organisations hope to strengthen the route from school participation into junior and adult club netball while also expanding opportunities in coaching, volunteering and leadership.

The partnership is expected to support new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing and volunteer development. The shared Rochdale AFC identity could also open up additional opportunities for sponsorship, commercial support, community events and promotion through the football club.

Amy Williams, Chair of Rochdale AFC Netball, described the move as a fantastic opportunity for both the club and the sport locally, saying joining the Rochdale AFC family would provide a stronger platform to grow the game and inspire more women and girls to become involved.

Rochdale AFC chief executive Laura Thomas, herself a former netball player, said she was thrilled to welcome the club into the wider Rochdale AFC family and stressed that the club's ambition to build a thriving community extends beyond football.

Ryan Bradley, Community Director at Rochdale AFC Community Trust, said the football club, charity and netball club shared common values and could combine their respective strengths. He said bringing the organisations together under one brand would raise netball's profile in Rochdale and strengthen support for volunteers, coaches, community outreach and school work.

Rochdale AFC Netball will be based at Edgar Wood. The Community Trust also pointed to plans for the Community Football and Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee, saying the geographical proximity of the projects made closer cooperation a natural step.

The move follows a wider trend in British sport in which professional football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to increase visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the organisations say their approach will remain community focused and open to people of all ages.

Further information about Rochdale AFC Netball teams, programmes and opportunities to get involved is expected to be announced in due course.

articles.title: £12m plan aims to bring Storage World Middleton site back to life after devastating fire
articles.excerpt: A £12m rebirth bid has been launched for the Storage World site in Middleton, more than a year after a devastating fire destroyed the Old Hall Street facility.
articles.content_html:
A £12m bid to bring the Storage World site in Middleton back to life has been launched, marking a major potential investment in an important part of the town centre following last year's devastating fire.

The proposals concern the Storage World site on Old Hall Street, next to Middleton Arena. The former storage facility was badly damaged by a major blaze in June 2025, which burned for several days and led to demolition of the building. No injuries were reported, although customers and businesses suffered significant losses.

Place North West has reported that Storage World has now launched a £12m rebirth bid for the site. The move comes as regeneration work and planning for the wider Middleton town centre area continues.

Official Rochdale Development Agency updates show that the council and RDA have remained in discussions with Storage World since the fire. In June, the RDA said it was working with stakeholders to develop key principles for the area, including the potential to deliver improvements to Middleton Arena and create a new public space. It also confirmed that discussions with Storage World were continuing with input from Rochdale Borough Council's planning team.

The site is particularly significant because of its position beside Middleton Arena and within an area being considered as part of wider plans for the future of Middleton town centre. Earlier council reports said the outcomes of discussions over Storage World and the arena would feed into wider masterplanning work.

Before the fire, Storage World operated a large self-storage and workspace facility from Old Hall Street. The Middleton operation had previously expanded as demand grew, with the company providing traditional storage alongside space used by small and online businesses.

The 2025 blaze had a substantial impact on customers. Fire crews worked for days at the scene and parts of the building were demolished while firefighting operations were still under way to allow crews safe access. Storage World said at the time that its team was devastated by the impact on customers and the wider community.

The latest £12m proposal therefore represents a potentially significant next chapter for a prominent town-centre site and comes at a time when Middleton is the subject of wider regeneration and masterplanning proposals.

Rochdale Daily will update this story as further planning documents and details of the proposed redevelopment become publicly available.

articles.title: Rochdale businesses urged to back Denehurst House in £30-a-month veterans challenge
articles.excerpt: Get Together After Serving CIC is calling on 100 local businesses to pledge £30 a month to help keep Denehurst House operational and support veterans in need.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale veterans organisation has launched a drive to recruit 100 local businesses willing to contribute £30 a month towards the running of Denehurst House.

Get Together After Serving CIC, known as GTAS CIC, is promoting the Rochdale 100-Businesses Challenge as a way for firms across the borough to make a relatively small regular contribution which, collectively, could provide significant ongoing support.

Campaign material shared with Rochdale Daily says Denehurst House provides support for veterans including emergency housing, hot meals, company and mental-health support. The organisation describes the building as a lifeline for former service personnel at times when they may be facing isolation, housing difficulties or other pressures.

The campaign is asking for 100 businesses to pledge £30 each month. If all 100 places are filled, that would amount to £3,000 a month in regular support for the project, or £36,000 over a full year if every pledge remained in place.

GTAS CIC says the purpose of the challenge is not simply to raise money, but to create a lasting partnership between local employers, traders and the veterans community. Its campaign artwork highlights volunteering, shared meals and local business involvement under the message that stronger community links can create a real impact.

Denehurst House is presented by the organisation as a base where veterans can find practical help as well as human contact. The campaign stresses the value of warm meals and company alongside emergency accommodation and mental-health support, reflecting the reality that a person in crisis may need several forms of help at the same time.

For businesses, the proposition is deliberately simple: £30 a month, with the combined backing of 100 companies intended to provide a more predictable stream of funding than one-off donations alone. That regularity can be particularly important for community organisations which have to meet continuing costs while responding to people whose needs cannot always be predicted in advance.

The challenge also gives Rochdale firms an opportunity to support a project rooted in the borough and aimed specifically at people who have served in the Armed Forces. GTAS CIC's message to businesses is that even a modest individual contribution can become substantial when it is repeated across a large local network.

The organisation is now seeking companies of all sizes to take part. Businesses interested in joining the Rochdale 100-Businesses Challenge are being asked to contact GTAS CIC by email at hello@gtascic.co.uk.

Rochdale Daily will update this article if further information is supplied on the progress of the campaign, the number of businesses signed up or the work being supported through the scheme.

articles.title: Videos raise hygiene concerns at one-star Halifax Road halal meat shop
articles.excerpt: Videos circulating on social media have prompted questions about food hygiene at Rajdhani Halal Meats on Halifax Road, which is listed with a one-star food hygiene rating.
articles.content_html:
Videos circulating on social media have prompted fresh questions about food hygiene at Rajdhani Halal Meats, 115 Halifax Road, Rochdale, after footage was shared which appears to show meat being handled outside close to commercial waste bins.

The footage has been discussed on local social-media groups, where residents have called for the circumstances to be investigated. Screenshots accompanying the posts show a person working behind the premises near large bins and commercial equipment. Rochdale Daily has not independently verified when the footage was recorded, exactly what type of meat was being handled, or whether the activity shown breached food-safety regulations.

Separate published food-hygiene information lists Rajdhani Halal Meats with a food hygiene rating of 1 — 'major improvement necessary' — following an inspection recorded on 25 June 2025.

A one-star food hygiene rating does not in itself establish that food currently being sold by a business is unsafe. It records the assessment made by inspectors at the time of the relevant inspection and businesses can make improvements or seek reassessment.

The circulating footage is nevertheless likely to prompt questions about whether further investigation or inspection is required. Food businesses are required to follow hygiene controls designed to protect food from contamination during storage, preparation and handling.

Residents concerned about food hygiene at a premises can report their concerns to the relevant local authority environmental-health service.

Rochdale Daily is inviting Rajdhani Halal Meats to explain the circumstances shown in the footage, including when it was recorded, what activity was taking place and whether any subsequent changes have been made.

The business is also invited to provide evidence of any more recent inspection or updated food-hygiene assessment. Any substantive response will be added prominently to this article.

articles.title: Thousands Attend Rochdale Feel Good Festival Featuring Gabrielle
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Feel Good Festival, held on 8 August 2026, attracted large crowds to the town centre, showcasing live music, food, and entertainment, with performances from Gabrielle and local bands.
articles.content_html:
Thousands gathered in Rochdale town centre on Saturday, 8 August 2026, for the annual Rochdale Feel Good Festival, which featured a vibrant mix of music, food, and entertainment. The event, organised by the Rochdale Development Agency, was headlined by two-time BRIT Award winner Gabrielle, alongside performances from Ash and Starsailor.

The festival kicked off in the early afternoon, with large crowds flocking to the main stage located in Rochdale Town Hall Square. Councillor Georgina Jacques, assistant cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council, expressed her delight at the turnout, noting that visitors from across the UK attended, many experiencing Rochdale for the first time. She remarked, "Gabrielle was excellent and I think her set was a fitting celebration by a much-loved star, with plenty of 90s nostalgia and uplifting vibes in a beautiful setting."

The main stage was opened by local metal band Metro, who won this year's Rochdale Music Service Battle of the Bands competition. Their performance received a warm reception from the audience, marking an impressive debut for the young band, which was formed just last year.

Following the festival, the Rochdale Development Agency will be gathering feedback and conducting a thorough evaluation of the event in the coming weeks. Councillor Jacques thanked everyone involved in the festival's success, including staff, partners, volunteers, and attendees.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Signs Midfielder Baba Adeeko from Wigan Athletic
articles.excerpt: Rochdale have secured the signing of midfielder Baba Adeeko from Wigan Athletic on a one-year contract as they prepare for their League Two campaign.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale have announced the signing of central midfielder Baba Adeeko from Wigan Athletic on a one-year deal. The 23-year-old joins the newly-promoted side ahead of their League Two campaign, which begins with a match against Newport County on Saturday at 12:30 BST.

Adeeko arrives at Spotland after spending five years with Wigan, where he made 98 appearances across all competitions. He made his first-team debut in a Carabao Cup tie in 2021 and has since accumulated 80 appearances in League One, demonstrating his capability at a competitive level.

Born in Galway, Adeeko has also represented the Republic of Ireland at Under-19 and Under-21 levels, showcasing his potential and experience at a young age. His background in the English leagues is expected to bolster Rochdale's midfield as they aim to establish themselves in League Two this season.

The signing of Adeeko is part of Rochdale's strategy to strengthen their squad following promotion, and fans will be eager to see how he contributes to the team's performance as they embark on their new campaign.

articles.title: Burnley Man Banned from Keeping Animals for 15 Years After Dog Found Neglected in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Paul Lewis Dawson, 37, has received a 15-year ban on keeping animals after pleading guilty to animal welfare offences involving a severely neglected dog found in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
ONGOING STORY — Updated 13 August 2026 at 22:58. 15 source updates have been combined into this article.

A 37-year-old man from Rochdale has been convicted of animal cruelty after his dog was found in a severely neglected condition. Paul Dawson was sentenced on August 13, 2026, after it was revealed that his dog, Kano, was starving, filthy, flea-ridden, and collapsing from anaemia.

The court heard that Dawson failed to provide adequate care for Kano, leading to the dog's distressing state. Despite the severity of the neglect, Dawson received a suspended sentence, which has raised concerns among animal welfare advocates about the adequacy of the punishment.

Animal welfare organisations have expressed outrage at the decision, highlighting the need for stricter penalties for animal cruelty cases. They argue that such leniency sends a troubling message regarding the treatment of animals.

As a result of this conviction, Dawson is likely to face scrutiny from local animal welfare groups, and there may be calls for increased awareness and education on responsible pet ownership in the Rochdale area.

The Trust said: “It’s all happening at St. Mary’s CE Primary School, Rochdale this summer; a real hive of activity as the hall and reception class are both having a makeover including new ceilings and acoustic baffles.

St Mary’s CE Primary School has served the Rochdale community for more than 150 years and is part of the Watergrove Trust, which brings together schools across the borough with a shared focus on school improvement and community provision.

The latest summer works continue that investment, with the refurbished spaces expected to be ready for the start of the new academic year in September.

articles.title: Can’t make it to church? Christ Church Healey invites community to join Sunday service online
articles.excerpt: Christ Church Healey is inviting people who cannot attend in person, are new to church or simply want to find out more to join its Sunday morning service online each week.
articles.content_html:
People across Healey and the wider Rochdale community who are unable to attend church in person are being warmly invited to join Christ Church's Sunday morning service online each week.

The church's weekly livestream is also open to people who may be new to church, curious about Christianity or who would simply feel more comfortable experiencing a service from home before deciding whether to attend in person.

Christ Church goes live at 9.55am every Sunday morning, allowing viewers to watch the service as it happens. Anyone who cannot watch at that time can catch up afterwards, with the service remaining available to view later.

The church said: “You are most welcome to join us for our weekly Sunday morning livestream from Christ Church. You can watch the service live as it happens, or at any time afterwards. We go live at 9.55am.”

For people who are housebound, unwell, caring for somebody, working on Sunday mornings or otherwise unable to be physically present, the livestream provides a way to remain connected with worship and the local church community.

It can also offer a gentle introduction for anyone who has never attended church before. There is no requirement to already be a member of the congregation — viewers can simply tune in from home and see what a Sunday morning at Christ Church is like.

The livestream runs each Sunday, with the broadcast beginning at 9.55am. Christ Church Healey welcomes both its existing congregation and newcomers joining online.

events.title: The Black Dyke Band at Rochdale Town Hall 2027

Since the post refurbishment of the Town Hall, the band have since gone on to perform every year bringing the best of brass band quality for all to enjoy. Join them again in 2027. Rochdale, Town Hall, The Esplanade, Rochdale
